quote: But experiment has shown that the more detailed subjects’ visualization, the more optimistic (and less accurate) they become.
content: Implementation intentions are not the thing the essay warns against, and the difference is the point of Gollwitzer’s own work. An implementation intention specifies when, where and how, and crucially what to do when an obstacle appears; the essay’s target is detailed visualization of the successful outcome, which the same research group found reduces achievement — students who fantasized positively about finding a job applied for fewer and got fewer offers (Oettingen & Mayer 2002). The literature distinguishes exactly where the essay distinguishes: plan the obstacles, do not picture the triumph, and never let either produce your date estimate.

quote: Are they symptoms of bureaucracy or government incentive failures? Yes, very probably.
content: Both causes are named in the essay, and the annotation quotes the sentence in which the second is conceded. They are also not competitors: Flyvbjerg’s own remedy for strategic misrepresentation is reference-class forecasting, which is the essay’s prescription, adopted because an outside-view number is hard for an interested promoter to manipulate. And the cognitive effect is not confined to students: it appears in professional software estimates, tax filings, and, in the original studies, in subjects predicting their own behavior with money at stake (Buehler, Griffin & Ross 1994). An essay introducing a bias to general readers is entitled to spend its length on the bias.
